A.depoimento: I have ordered the split of my starting army to assault the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora. By sending spearmen and archers to Santarem, and knights to Evora, I aim to secure two new resource-producing villages in a single turn. Meanwhile, the construction of two spearmen in the capital has been ordered to ensure its continued defense.

I am splitting my current forces to attack both villages simultaneously, leveraging the counter triangle (spearmen vs knights in Santarem, knights vs archers in Evora). I am also building 2 spearmen in Lisboa to maintain a capital garrison.

B.depoimento: We order the attack on the neutral villages. The army marches to claim Tarragona and Girona for King B.
B.plano: Capture Tarragona and Girona to expand. Keep a reserve at Barcelona. Next turn, build more troops and explore south towards Zaragoza and Huesca.

A.depoimento: I am striking at the neutral villages to secure my borders and increase my resource income. My spearman take Coimbra, archers take Badajoz, and knights take Faro. I am also reinforcing my capital with new spearmen.
A.plano: Capture Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro to expand my territory and resource production. Build 2 spearmen in Lisboa to maintain a capital garrison. Next turn, explore the road network to find more villages and the enemy.

A.plano: Gather all available troops in Badajoz to launch a decisive attack on Toledo next turn. Build spearmen across all interior villages and a knight in the capital to sustain the offensive. Send the archers from Sevilha and knights from Faro to reinforce the strike force.

B.depoimento: King B mobilizes his army! We send troops from the interior to the border, reinforcing Valencia and Zaragoza. Our blacksmiths work at full capacity, forging spears, archers, and knights. Next turn, we shall strike the neutral villages of Teruel and Madrid and expand our territory!

Build knights and archers in interior villages to feed the war machine. Do not attack yet; wait until we have overwhelming force with counter bonuses.

A.depoimento: Our armies strike Toledo this turn to break the neutral barrier and open the path to the enemy's heart. While the main force marches, our workers toil in the villages, forging spears and training knights to fuel the endless campaign. We will not stop until the enemy capital falls and the peninsula is ours.
A.plano: Attack Toledo with all troops from Badajoz. Build spearmen everywhere to replenish ranks. Send reinforcements from Santarem, Lisboa, and Evora to prepare for the next push towards Madrid and Cordoba. Keep building knights in Lisboa and Faro for future offensive power.

B.depoimento: We committed our spearmen to break the knight garrisons of Teruel and Madrid, while our interior villages marched to reinforce the border and secure the new territories.
B.plano: Launch spearman attacks on Teruel and Madrid to counter their knights. Reinforce Valencia and Zaragoza with interior troops. After capturing them, explore west and prepare archer attacks on Murcia and Pamplona.

A.depoimento: The king's knights and archers sweep through Cordoba, crushing the neutral archers with their counter tactics. Our forces press forward, and reinforcements flow to hold the new land. Toledo stands ready for any enemy challenge.

B.depoimento: King B here. I have fortified my borders against King A's forces. My archers are ready to counter their spearmen. I will not let them take my lands. The enemy will pay heavily if they attack.
B.plano: Fortified Madrid and Teruel with archers and spearmen to defend against King A's army from Toledo. Built archers in all interior villages for future attacks. Next turn, assess the battle results and attack neutral villages like Pamplona and Murcia with our new archers. Watch for enemy movements from unexplored territories.

Our domestic production is at maximum, with every village pumping out spearmen to swell our ranks. Reinforcements are marching to Toledo and Coimbra to secure our borders and prepare for the next push into enemy territory.
A.plano: We are attacking Murcia with archers and knights to exploit the counter bonus against their spearmen. We are building spearmen in all villages to grow our army. We are reinforcing Toledo and Coimbra to prepare for future attacks on Madrid and Salamanca. Next turn, we will assess the results of the Murcia attack and the enemy's movement toward Teruel.

B.depoimento: This turn our armies struck in two places: a strong force from Madrid took Burgos, and Huesca's entire army captured Pamplona. We have brought our village count to 11. Reinforcements from Zaragoza and Tarragona march to Madrid to secure the new western border, while Valencia begins building for the next push into Murcia.

We reinforce Madrid with archers from Zaragoza and a knight from Tarragona, and move Castellon's troops to Valencia to prepare for the Murcia attack. Interior villages build archers and knights for future growth. Watch for enemy counterattacks and arrival of reinforcements.

A.depoimento: I have launched a two-pronged attack on Valencia and Porto to expand my territory. I have also reinforced my border villages, especially Toledo, and begun building a large force of knights to challenge Madrid. My army is growing, and I aim to secure more villages to reach the 18 needed for victory.
A.plano: We are attacking Valencia with archers and a knight to exploit the counter bonus against their spearmen. We are also attacking Porto to gain another village. We are reinforcing Toledo with knights and spearmen from multiple villages to prepare for a future attack on Madrid. We are building knights and archers across our villages to grow our army. We decided NOT to attack Madrid yet because we lack enough knights to counter their archers effectively.

B.depoimento: Our army struck at Salamanca to claim the neutral village, while we shored up Madrid's defenses. Troops from the interior marched to the front, and we built knights across the realm to fuel our expansion.
B.plano: Attacking Salamanca with 3 spearmen and 1 knight from Madrid, leaving all 6 archers for defense. Reinforcing Madrid with archers from Zaragoza and troops from Burgos. Consolidating interior troops: Tarragona and Huesca send troops to Zaragoza, Barcelona to Tarragona, Girona to Huesca, Castellon to Valencia. Building knights in all villages. Next turn: assess Salamanca and Pamplona battles, reinforce Pamplona, and plan attack on Vigo or western villages.

A.depoimento: Today, I ordered a double strike! From Coimbra, I send a strong spear and knight force to finally conquer Salamanca, which has been a thorn in our side. Simultaneously, from our mighty fortress of Toledo, I launch a decisive blow against Madrid, sending a powerful knight-led army to break their archers and claim the enemy capital's gateway. My blacksmiths are working overtime, forging knights and spearmens to replenish our ranks and ensure our empire's dominance!
A.plano: We are attacking Salamanca from Coimbra with 5 spearmen and 1 knight to conquer our 12th village. We are also attacking Madrid from Toledo with 5 knights and 4 spearmen to exploit the counter bonus against their archers and conquer a major enemy hub. We are building knights and spearmen across our villages to grow our army and replace losses. We decided NOT to attack Valencia yet because we need to reinforce Murcia first.

B.depoimento: We are setting up our staging grounds for a major push next turn. By reinforcing Burgos, Salamanca, and Valencia, we are preparing to conquer Vigo, Badajoz, and Murcia respectively. Our interior production is focused on building knights and shuttling troops to the borders. If successful, this will bring our village count to 15, putting us closer to the 18 needed for victory.
B.plano: Consolidating troops for a triple offensive next turn. Madrid is sending archers and knights to Burgos (to attack Vigo) and Salamanca (to attack Badajoz). Teruel is reinforcing Valencia for the attack on Murcia. Zaragoza is reinforcing Madrid, while Tarragona and Huesca reinforce Zaragoza. Building knights in all capable villages to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: This turn, we focused on consolidation and reinforcement. Our army marching on Madrid has the upper hand against the archer-heavy garrison, and we are sending 21 spearmen from Toledo to secure the city once it falls. We are reinforcing Coimbra from Porto to offset the expected losses at Salamanca, and we are strengthening Murcia from Cordoba to guard against Valencia. Across our realm, we are busy producing knights and spearmen to build the strongest army possible for the campaigns ahead.
A.plano: We are focusing on reinforcing our positions and preparing for the conquest of Madrid. Our main attack on Madrid with 5 knights and 4 spearmen should succeed due to the knight-archer counter bonus. We are sending 21 spearmen from Toledo to Madrid to secure it as our 12th village and establish a strong garrison. We are reinforcing Coimbra with 5 spearmen from Porto to replace the losses from the failed attack on Salamanca. We are also reinforcing Murcia from Cordoba to protect our eastern border. We are building a mix of knights and spearman across all our villages to grow our army for the next

B.depoimento: Turn 10: We launch a three-pronged offensive! Burgos takes the neutral Vigo, Valencia crushes Murcia, and Salamanca's archers snatch Coimbra. Simultaneously, we shuffle reinforcements to the frontlines: Madrid sends troops to Salamanca, Zaragoza reinforces Madrid, and Teruel bolsters Valencia. Our war machines keep turning as we build knights and archers across the realm. The enemy attacks on Madrid and Salamanca are met with steady garrisons, and we press the advantage!
B.plano: Attacking Vigo, Murcia, and Coimbra this turn to gain 3 villages. Sending reinforcements from Madrid to Salamanca, Zaragoza to Madrid, and Teruel to Valencia to prepare for next turn's offensive on Badajoz and Porto. Building knights and archers everywhere to sustain the momentum and replenish losses.

A.depoimento: We are reinforcing our positions and gathering troops for the next major assaults. The 21 spearmen are marching to Madrid to secure it. We are sending reinforcements to Porto, Toledo, and Murcia to prepare for the conquest of Vigo, Teruel, and Valencia. Our army is growing steadily as we build across all villages.
A.plano: We are focusing on reinforcing our borders and preparing for the conquest of Madrid, Vigo, and Teruel. Our main attack on Madrid with 21 spearmen should succeed. We are sending troops from Coimbra to Porto to prepare for the attack on Vigo, and from Badajoz to Toledo to prepare for Teruel. We are also reinforcing Murcia from Cordoba to protect our eastern border. We are building a mix of knights and spearman across all our villages to grow our army.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launched a coordinated assault: our knights strike Vigo from Santarem, while our Madrid spearman march on Burgos. We are reinforcing our borders heavily, sending troops to Madrid, Toledo, Coimbra, Badajoz, and beyond. Our villages are building knights to grow our might. We are confident these moves will secure our empire!
A.plano: Plan: Attack Vigo with 6 knights from Santarem and Burgos with 11 spearman from Madrid. Reinforce Madrid (5s from Toledo), Toledo (2k from Sevilha), Coimbra (3s from Santarem), Badajoz (4k from Evora), Santarem (4s from Lisboa), Cordoba (2k from Sevilha), Sevilha (2k from Faro). Build knights everywhere. Next turn: assess losses, reinforce new villages, plan attacks on Salamanca/Teruel.

B.depoimento: We are launching a decisive attack on the weak enemy village of Badajoz from Salamanca. We are building as many knights and archers as possible and consolidating our forces on the borders to prepare for the next wave of conquests. Our goal is to capture Badajoz and use it as a stepping stone to conquer the rest of the enemy's territory.

Next turn, reinforce Badajoz with newly built archers from Salamanca. Consolidate forces on border villages by sending interior troops to Zaragoza, Valencia, and Burgos.

A.depoimento: Today, my armies strike on three fronts! The knights of Vigo and Badajoz march to conquer Burgos and Salamanca, while the elite garrison of Murcia, reinforced with fresh archers, launches a decisive assault on Valencia. I have ordered the construction of knights and archers across the realm to replenish our ranks and prepare for the next push into enemy territory. The enemy's defenses will shatter!
A.plano: Attack Burgos (5k from Vigo), Salamanca (5k from Badajoz), Valencia (7s, 3a, 2k from Murcia after building 1 archer). Build knights in Vigo, Badajoz, Cordoba, Sevilha, Porto, and others to replenish. Next turn, reinforce Murcia from Cordoba, Vigo from Porto, Badajoz from Sevilha. Prepare archers in Toledo and Madrid for Teruel.

I am reinforcing Zaragoza with knights from my interior villages and sending knights from Burgos and Salamanca to garrison Madrid after the victory. I am building 10 knights and 5 archers across my villages to expand my army for the next push.

In a massive mobilization, we marched our interior armies to the front lines, reinforcing Salamanca, Toledo, Murcia, and Burgos. Our troops are now positioned to launch a triple offensive next turn against Madrid, Teruel, and Valencia, which should bring us to our target of 18 villages.
A.plano: Attack Pamplona with 2 knights from Burgos to secure an easy village. Move all interior troops to border villages (Salamanca, Toledo, Murcia, Burgos) to prepare for a coordinated offensive next turn. Build troops in every village to replenish forces. Next turn, attack Madrid from Salamanca, Teruel from Toledo, and Valencia from Murcia to reach 18 villages.

B.depoimento: I'm striking hard at the enemy's weakest points this turn. Murcia is practically defenseless, and Salamanca and Burgos are reeling from recent combat. With Madrid's knights leading the charge, I expect to capture all three and push my holdings to 13 villages. The archers I'm building everywhere will fuel the next wave of conquests.

Keep 5 knights + 4 archers in Madrid for defense. Build max archers everywhere and 1 knight at Madrid to replenish losses. Next turn: consider attacking Toledo from reinforced Teruel, and push toward the unexplored southern villages.

B.depoimento: I have launched a double attack on Vigo and Pamplona, reinforcing Burgos to secure the border. My armies are on the march to conquer two more villages this turn, bringing me closer to the 18-victory threshold.
B.plano: Attack Vigo from Burgos with 3 knights, and Pamplona from Zaragoza with 4 knights. Reinforce Burgos with 2 archers from Madrid to defend against Pamplona. Build max archers everywhere and knights where possible. Next turn, consolidate gains and prepare attacks on Salamanca and Toledo.

The elite knights of Salamanca and Cordoba are marching to Madrid and Murcia respectively, aiming to crush the enemy's defenses and expand our territory. Simultaneously, I am reinforcing our border villages and building up our forces across the kingdom to ensure we are ready for the next assault.
A.plano: Launch a double attack on Madrid and Murcia to secure the borders. Send all available troops from Salamanca to Madrid, and Cordoba to Murcia. Reinforce Salamanca and Toledo with troops from Badajoz, and Cordoba with troops from Sevilha. Build knights in all villages to prepare for the next wave of attacks on Vigo and Teruel.

Reinforce Madrid with 6 knights from Toledo to defend against the incoming enemy army and prepare for the next wave of attacks. Build knights in all possible villages to maximize cavalry production for the next turn's offensive.

Porto is being reinforced to hold the west while I set up a double strike on Coimbra and Salamanca next turn. Teruel and Valencia are getting reinforcements to hold against expected enemy attacks, and Burgos is being built up to strike Madrid after Girona's army weakens it. Building archers and knights in every village to feed the fronts.

Reinforce Burgos, Coimbra, Salamanca, and Valencia for next turn. Build spearmen and knights everywhere to grow the army. Next turn, assess results and plan attacks on Vigo and Pamplona; watch for enemy counterattacks on Coimbra and Valencia.

Zaragoza is now a fortress, receiving nearly twenty reinforcements from Teruel, Tarragona, and Huesca. My interior villages are stripped to reinforce the borders, and every village is building troops for the next wave. The path to eighteen villages is open; the next turn will decide it.

A.plano: Attack Vigo from Porto and Castellon from Valencia with knights to conquer them and reach 18 villages. Reinforce Zaragoza from Madrid and Valencia from Murcia to defend against enemy counterattacks. Build knights and spearmen across the empire to grow the army.

We launched an attack on Valencia from Castellon, hoping to expand our territory while our main army takes Zaragoza. We kept our other forces on guard, expecting the enemy to strike our vulnerable frontiers.

Keeping other troops in place to defend, especially Vigo, Pamplona, Tarragona, Huesca. The marching army from Teruel should take Zaragoza next turn. Build knights and archers across the empire. Next turn, focus on defending Burgos against Pamplona and try to conquer another village to reach 18. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Madrid and Valencia.

On turn 22, attack Tarragona from Castellon with all troops (1 spear, 6 knights), and attack Pamplona from Burgos with 4 knights and 2 archers (leave 4 spearmen for defense). This should conquer both villages, bringing my total to 19. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Madrid and Valencia.

I am sending my full available forces from Tarragona, Zaragoza, Teruel, and Pamplona. Additionally, I am building knights and archers in all my villages to prepare for the next turn's consolidation.
B.plano: Launch a massive 4-front offensive to retake Castellon and conquer Madrid, Valencia, and Burgos simultaneously. Build knights and archers in all my villages to reinforce them for the next turn. Do not attack Toledo yet as it is too strong.

B.depoimento: We launched a coordinated offensive on two fronts, taking Castellon and Murcia with ease. At the same time, we heavily reinforced Burgos to prepare for the push into Vigo, while sending troops to Madrid and Valencia to secure our borders. The net is closing on King A's territory!

Simultaneously, from Madrid, I sent a strong force to attack Salamanca, leveraging the archer counter to overcome its defenses. I kept a small garrison in Madrid to guard against a sudden strike from Toledo. On the production side, I focused on building knights across almost all my villages to ensure my army remains technologically superior and ready for the next wave of conquests.

Keep some troops in Madrid to defend against potential Toledo attack. Next turn, reinforce Madrid and Murcia, and prepare to attack Porto, Coimbra, or Cordoba.

Coimbra's spear and knight take Salamanca, Toledo's archers fall upon Teruel while its knights ride to Madrid, and Sevilha's host marches on Murcia. Every village is building knights for the next wave. The enemy capital is not my goal; I will win by taking every village they have.

Next turn, use the newly captured villages as springboards to attack Vigo, Zaragoza, and Valencia. Always check counter matchups: use knights against archer-heavy garrisons and spearmen against knight-heavy ones.

We also reinforce Madrid and Burgos to secure our borders and build knights in our key cities to prepare for the next wave of expansion.

Reinforce Madrid with troops from Zaragoza and Burgos, and reinforce Burgos from Pamplona to secure our western flank. Next turn, focus on conquering Badajoz and Coimbra from Salamanca, and Toledo from Madrid/Teruel.

Valencia sends reinforcements to Murcia to secure our southern border. We build up our armies across all territories, aiming to reach 18 villages and secure our victory.

Build knights in major cities and archers in border cities. Next turn, consolidate gains and prepare for attacks on Badajoz and Toledo.

Murcia marched on Valencia, and Teruel sent its troops to reinforce Zaragoza for the push into Pamplona and Tarragona. Cordoba and Sevilha began troop movements to bolster the central front. Sevilha sends troops to Cordoba to build up the central front. Build troops in all villages to replenish losses and maintain momentum. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Salamanca and Toledo.

This turn, we are launching a coordinated counter-offensive on the eastern front to reclaim Zaragoza and Teruel, carefully matching our troop types to the enemy's to exploit the counter triangle. We are also reinforcing our newly gained Madrid and the Tarragona border to secure our heartlands. We will not let the enemy push us back!

Reinforce Madrid from Burgos and Tarragona from Barcelona to secure our new central territories. Do not attack Murcia or Salamanca yet as they are heavily reinforced. Build archers and spearmen in border villages, and spearmen in Porto for the Coimbra push.
